snippet.description:
Master Euler's Theorem for Homogeneous Functions in Engineering Mathematics, Calculus, BSc Maths. Learn Homogeneous Function degree, partial differentiation & full Euler Theorem proof step by step.

Is video lecture mein hum detail mein cover karenge Euler's Theorem on Homogeneous Functions (समघात फलनों के लिए आइलर प्रमेय). Agar aap BSc Maths, BTech / Engineering Mathematics ya kisi competitive exam ki preparation kar rahe hain, toh yeh topic aapke Calculus syllabus ka ek essential part hai.

📌 Topics Covered in This Video:

What is a Homogeneous Function? (समघात फलन क्या होता है?)
How to find the Degree of a Homogeneous Function (n-degree identification)
Euler's Theorem Statement for 2 Variables
Step-by-Step Proof of Euler's Theorem: $x \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} + y \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = nz$
Second-Order Partial Derivative Extension & Proof
Euler's Theorem Extension for 3 Variables & $m$ Variables

Timestamps:
00:00 – Recap & Introduction to Euler's Relation
02:18 – Intuitive Concept of Homogeneous Functions
05:16 – Definition & Degree of Homogeneous Functions (Scaling Method)
07:26 – General Definition for Algebraic & Transcendental Functions
09:02 – Example: Checking Homogeneity & Finding Degree
10:48 – Non-Homogeneous Function Example & Explanation
12:18 – Transcendental Homogeneous Function Example
13:10 – Euler's Theorem Statement (Two Variables)
15:04 – Step-by-Step Proof of Euler's Theorem
21:08 – Euler's Theorem for Second-Order Partial Derivatives (Corollary)
23:40 – Proof of Second-Order Form & Deductions
33:45 – Extension of Euler's Theorem for $m$ Variables & 3 Variables
37:37 – Summary, Key Takeaways & What's Next

🎓 Yeh Video Kin Ke Liye Useful Hai:
🔸B.Sc, B.Sc B.Ed, Maths students 
🔸B.Tech Engineering Maths 
🔸GATE Mathematics 
🔸IIT JAM Mathematics

🔗 Previous Lecture:
Partial Differentiation: Second Order Derivatives & Mixed Derivatives→ https://youtu.be/3latY9y4OoU

📚 RECOMMENDED BOOKS / STUDY MATERIAL
If you want to study this topic in more depth, the following books are very helpful:

📘 Thomas' Calculus (15th Edition) – George B. Thomas, Maurice D. Weir & Joel R. Hass
👉 https://amzn.to/48DQjQW

📘 Single Variable Calculus (Hardcover) – James Stewart
👉 https://amzn.to/4cQeZbk

📘 Differential Calculus – Shanti Narayan & P.K. Mittal
👉 https://amzn.to/4cRttb2

📘 Integral Calculus – Shanti Narayan & P.K. Mittal
👉 https://amzn.to/4cReFsT

📘 Calculus, Vol. 1: One-Variable Calculus, with an Introduction to Linear Algebra – Tom M. Apostol
👉 https://amzn.to/4mBuoQ9

📘Higher Engineering Mathematics — B.S. Grewal
👉 https://amzn.to/4cz7dS7

📘Advanced Engineering Mathematics — Erwin Kreyszig
👉 https://amzn.to/41FY1pW

📘 Mathematical Methods for Physics and Engineering — K.F. Riley
👉 https://amzn.to/42cW0Sf

📘 Schaum’s Outline of Calculus
👉 https://amzn.to/4u0oxqd
